title: test-integration-others-internal barrier group (the ~19+ non-ISS-503 test-integration binaries) still deadlock (40P01) against each other under full concurrent `zig build test-integration`, independent of ISS-0106's ISS-503 fix
category_note: CATEGORY B (Integration/DB error) per docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 1. Entirely within the DB/migration-test integration layer (Postgres lock contention among concurrently-running test-integration binaries); no application/business-logic code path implicated.
category_detail: test-isolation / postgres-lock-contention-under-concurrent-DDL (scoped to the non-ISS-503 sibling group)
notes:
Discovered by BACKEND-DEV while validating the ISS-0106 fix (GitHub #364), which serializes ONLY tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig out of the concurrent `test-integration` group via a new `test_integration_others_step` barrier (see build.zig and src/design/fix-ISS-0106.md). ISS-0106's design explicitly scoped its fix to the ISS-503-vs-others concurrency window only, and explicitly stated as a non-goal: 'the ~19+ *other* binaries remain fully concurrent with each other -- this design narrows the fix to exactly the one binary ISSUE-FIXER identified as the DDL-lock-holding offender. It does not serialize the whole suite.'

Across three independent, clean full `zig build test-integration` runs performed to validate ISS-0106 (each starting from a freshly-migrated, empty-row test database, with no other process touching the DB concurrently), the `test_integration_others_step` barrier itself (i.e. the ~19+ non-ISS-503 binaries running concurrently with each other, exactly as they did before ISS-0106) consistently failed with genuine Postgres `deadlock detected` (40P01) errors: run3 showed 14 deadlocks, run4 showed 10, run5 showed 4 -- always among the OTHER binaries (e.g. exp103_instance_waits_test.zig, tnt_schema_isolation_test.zig, iss205_webhook_outbox_test.zig, and the umbrella's own db_integration_test.zig via TestHarness.init()/runMigrations()), never involving test_iss503_rls_removal.zig (zero hits for 'iss503'/'ISS503'/'test_iss503' in any of the three run logs -- confirming ISS-0106's fix works: ISS-503 is correctly gated behind the barrier and is never reached until the barrier settles, whether the barrier's own members pass or fail).

Because the barrier step's completion is a precondition for `run_iss503_integration_tests_after_others` (and hence for `test_integration_step` overall) under Zig's build-step semantics, a failure inside the barrier propagates as a `test-integration` umbrella failure even though ISS-503 itself never ran and never faulted. This means db_integration_test.zig's TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 (the original #357/ISS-0100/ISS-0105/ISS-0106 acceptance-bar tests) still fail under a full `zig build test-integration` run -- but the failure signature has changed: it is now caused by deadlocks among the OTHER concurrent binaries (relations repeatedly involved across runs: Postgres relation OIDs 17709/17770/17827/17878, corresponding to public-schema tables touched by multiple binaries' independent TestHarness.init()/runMigrations() calls), not by ISS-503's previously-proven AccessExclusiveLock-holding raw-connection DDL transactions racing the rest of the group.

This is a genuinely separate, pre-existing condition: ISS-0106's diff (build.zig + tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig doc comment only) never touches the relative concurrency of the ~19+ other binaries, so this deadlock pattern among them was already present on `main` before ISS-0106 and is unaffected by it in either direction. It was simply easier to observe in isolation once ISS-503 was no longer also contributing to the same failure signature.
candidate_resolution: Candidate directions (non-exclusive, needs its own WF-03 investigation to pick): (a) extend the same advisory-lock pattern already used in tests/integration/helpers.zig's runMigrations()/runForSchema() ('bpm_test_migrations_public' / per-schema keyed locks) so that ALL public-schema-touching binaries -- not just the migration bootstrap path -- serialize around DDL-heavy sections identified as deadlock-prone (would need a targeted audit of which of the ~19+ binaries perform DDL vs. pure DML); (b) apply a similar barrier/serialization strategy to ISS-0106's, but for a curated sub-group of the ~19+ binaries proven to deadlock against each other (rather than the whole group against ISS-503 alone) -- narrower and more surgical than serializing the entire suite; (c) investigate whether increasing Postgres's `deadlock_timeout` or adding a bounded client-side retry-on-40P01 wrapper around TestHarness.init() specifically (NOT a workaround for ISS-0106's proven root cause, but a legitimate mitigation for genuine resource contention among otherwise-independent binaries) is acceptable per this repo's no-retry-workaround convention -- likely needs explicit product/architecture sign-off since it cuts against the 'fix root cause, not symptom' principle applied in ISS-0106. Needs its own root-cause diagnosis identifying exactly which binary pairs collide and on which relations before choosing a resolution.
root_cause:
DEFINITIVE (source-verified 2026-07-31 by ISSUE-FIXER via a fresh full `zig build test-integration` reproduction, run_id WF03-iss0107-20260731). The relation OIDs recorded when ISS-0107 was filed (17709/17770/17827/17878) no longer exist -- the test DB has been recreated/re-migrated since -- so they were re-derived live in this run. The CURRENT deadlocked relations, confirmed via `SELECT oid, relname, relnamespace::regnamespace FROM pg_class WHERE oid IN (...)` against the running db_test container (port 5434) immediately after reproducing the deadlocks, are: oid 304530 = tenant_default.instance_projections, oid 304591 = tenant_default.process_definitions, oid 304609 = tenant_default.instance_definition_snapshots, oid 304648 = tenant_default.tasks. All four are business tables inside the shared `tenant_default` schema that every one of the ~19+ test-integration binaries provisions and writes into.

MECHANISM (source-verified against tests/integration/helpers.zig): TestHarness.init() (the shared bootstrap called by literally every test-integration binary, including exp103_instance_waits_test.zig indirectly via its own makePool(), tnt_schema_isolation_test.zig, iss205_webhook_outbox_test.zig, and db_integration_test.zig's own TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02) calls, in this exact order: (1) runMigrations() -- WRAPPED in `SELECT pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('bpm_test_migrations_public'))` (helpers.zig line 99); (2) runMigrationsForSchema(..., 'tenant_default', ...) -- WRAPPED in a per-schema advisory lock keyed by `hashtext($1)` where $1='tenant_default' (helpers.zig line 144); (3) configureTestSearchPath(); (4) resetTestData() -- **COMPLETELY UNPROTECTED**, issues `TRUNCATE TABLE instance_definition_snapshots, tasks, instance_projections, ..., process_definitions ... RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE` one table at a time (helpers.zig lines 306-322); (5) ensureDefaultOidcSeeds() -- unprotected DML; (6) applyCompatibilityShims() -- **COMPLETELY UNPROTECTED**, issues `DROP TRIGGER`/`CREATE TRIGGER`/`DROP FUNCTION`/`CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` DDL against `events` and `repository_artifacts` (helpers.zig lines 208-296). Both advisory locks are released (step 1's via `defer`) BEFORE steps 4-6 run, so by the time TRUNCATE/DDL executes, the calling process holds NO advisory lock at all. Since Migrations.run()/runForSchema() (src/db/migrations.zig) also contain no internal locking of their own -- confirmed by reading the full function bodies, lines 53-140 -- the advisory lock is entirely a helpers.zig caller-side convention that stops at step 3. Steps 4 and 6 run fully concurrently across all ~19+ binaries with zero cross-process ordering.

This live-reproduced run captured 21+ distinct 'deadlock detected' (40P01) Postgres errors, and every single one names relation OIDs from the set {304530, 304591, 304609, 304648} -- i.e. EXACTLY the four tables resetTestData() truncates (instance_projections, process_definitions, instance_definition_snapshots, tasks) -- in circular AccessExclusiveLock/RowShareLock/AccessShareLock wait chains among 3 concurrently-running test-integration processes at a time (e.g. 'Process 23325 waits for AccessExclusiveLock on relation 304530 (instance_projections); blocked by process 23309. Process 23309 waits for AccessExclusiveLock on relation 304648 (tasks); blocked by process 23538. Process 23538 waits for AccessExclusiveLock on relation 304530; blocked by process 23325.' -- a textbook N-way TRUNCATE-vs-TRUNCATE circular wait, since Postgres serializes each process's per-table lock acquisition order differently depending on scheduling). These deadlocks co-occur in the same log windows as corroborating unprotected-DDL symptoms from applyCompatibilityShims(), e.g. `trigger "trg_bpm_test_events_compat_defaults" for relation "events" already exists` (C42710) and `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "pg_proc_proname_args_nsp_index" ... (bpm_repository_artifacts_immutable, ...)` (C23505) -- both are exactly the race symptoms expected when multiple processes run `DROP ... IF EXISTS` + `CREATE ...` for the same trigger/function name with no mutual exclusion, and one process's DROP interleaves with another's CREATE.

This is DDL-vs-DDL contention (TRUNCATE-vs-TRUNCATE across binaries, plus a secondary DROP/CREATE-TRIGGER-vs-DROP/CREATE-TRIGGER race), not DDL-vs-DML: every colliding operation identified in the deadlock log details is itself a TRUNCATE (which Postgres always promotes to AccessExclusiveLock, never a lesser mode) issued by resetTestData(), not a normal business-logic INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT from test bodies. The advisory lock pattern already in helpers.zig is proven to work correctly for what it protects (steps 1-2, the actual migration check-and-apply passes) -- TEST-RUNNER's ISS-0106 verification and this run both show zero 'already exists'-style migration-file collisions -- but its scope was always narrower than 'the full TestHarness.init() sequence', and steps 4 and 6 were never brought under it.
chosen_resolution:
RESOLUTION: extend candidate (a) -- the SAME advisory-lock pattern already proven correct in helpers.zig for runMigrations()/runMigrationsForSchema() -- to cover the ENTIRE TestHarness.init() body, not just the migration check-and-apply passes. Concretely: widen the existing 'bpm_test_migrations_public' session advisory lock's held duration (or introduce one new dedicated lock key, e.g. 'bpm_test_harness_init', to avoid conflating migration semantics with harness-reset semantics) so that resetTestData() and applyCompatibilityShims() execute while the calling process holds the lock, and release it only after both have completed -- i.e. move the `defer conn.exec("SELECT pg_advisory_unlock(...)")` from immediately after runMigrations()'s own body (helpers.zig line 100) to wrap the full init() sequence through applyCompatibilityShims(), OR equivalently take a second advisory lock in TestHarness.init() itself around steps 4+6 (resetTestData/applyCompatibilityShims) using the same hashtext() keying convention already established at lines 99 and 144. Because TestHarness.init() is the single shared chokepoint every one of the ~19+ binaries already calls, this is a ONE-FILE change (tests/integration/helpers.zig only) -- it does not require touching each binary individually, keeping the fix well within the <=5 file Fix Scope Rule.

WHY (b) -- A CURATED build.zig BARRIER SUB-GROUP -- IS REJECTED HERE: unlike ISS-0106's ISS-503, where exactly ONE binary (a raw-connection outlier that bypasses helpers.zig entirely) was the proven offender and every other binary was innocent, THIS deadlock storm implicates the SHARED bootstrap path used by ALL ~19+ binaries symmetrically -- there is no minority sub-group to carve out; every binary that calls TestHarness.init() is equally a participant on both sides of every captured deadlock pair (e.g. iss208_task_guard_test, iss0091_harness_tracker_unification_test, tnt_schema_isolation_test all appear as both 'process waits for' and 'blocked by' across different deadlock instances in this run's log). Serializing 19 binaries against each other via a build-graph barrier would collapse test-integration's concurrency entirely, which is a far more expensive and architecturally heavier change than fixing the actual gap in an already-existing, already-proven locking mechanism. (b) is the right tool when one identifiable minority is the offender (as ISS-0106 correctly used it); it is the wrong tool when the offending code path is the shared majority-use helper itself.

WHY (c) -- RETRY/TIMEOUT WORKAROUNDS -- IS REJECTED: the root cause is structurally eliminable (widen an existing, already-correct locking mechanism to cover the two unprotected steps) rather than genuine unavoidable resource contention between independent actors, so a retry-on-40P01 wrapper would mask the symptom instead of closing the actual concurrency window, matching the same 'fix root cause, not symptom' principle ISS-0106 already established as this repo's convention. No further investigation of (c) is warranted since (a)-extended is proven sufficient and low-risk (same primitive, same call site, already battle-tested for steps 1-2).
files_to_change_note: Single-file fix. tests/integration/helpers.zig's TestHarness.init(): widen the existing 'bpm_test_migrations_public' advisory lock (or add one new dedicated lock acquired inside init()) so it is held across resetTestData() and applyCompatibilityShims() in addition to the migration passes it already covers, then released once both complete. No other file requires changes: Migrations.run()/runForSchema() (src/db/migrations.zig) were re-read in full during this investigation and confirmed to still correctly contain no locking of their own by design (locking is intentionally the caller's responsibility per the existing helpers.zig doc comments) -- extending helpers.zig's own lock scope is consistent with that existing design, not a deviation from it. build.zig requires no changes: this is not a build-graph/barrier problem (see chosen_resolution's rejection of candidate (b)). Stays within the <=5 file Fix Scope Rule (1 of 5).
verification_result: FAIL (WF03-iss0107-20260731, BACKEND-DEV, 2026-08-01). Implemented shape (1) exactly as specified in src/design/fix-ISS-0107.md: widened the bpm_test_migrations_public advisory lock in TestHarness.init() to cover configureTestSearchPath()+resetTestData()+ensureDefaultOidcSeeds()+applyCompatibilityShims(), released via an explicit pg_advisory_unlock call immediately after applyCompatibilityShims() completes (not a defer, to match the design's required release point before bpm.api_tenant_context.set()/conn.begin()). zig build and zig build test both pass (exit 0). 3 full zig build test-integration runs performed. RESULT: the original 40P01 deadlock storm in the TestHarness.init() bootstrap path (resetTestData()/applyCompatibilityShims() racing across ~19+ binaries) IS eliminated -- deadlock count trended 22 (documented baseline) -> 1 -> 2 -> 0 across the 3 runs, and the 1-2 residual deadlocks that did occur in runs 1-2 were confirmed via relation-OID and stack-trace inspection to be in UNRELATED business-logic code (exp103_instance_waits_test TaskStore.createInTx, audit_iss103_test trigger writes) -- not in the widened critical section. HOWEVER, a NEW failure mode was surfaced that the design did not anticipate: serializing ~19+ binaries through one widened critical section means queue depth/wait time grows, and configureSessionTimeouts() (helpers.zig, called earlier in the same TestHarness.init()) sets `lock_timeout = '5s'` on every connection -- so once enough binaries queue behind the widened lock, later waiters' own `pg_advisory_lock(hashtext(...))` acquire statement is itself cancelled by Postgres with 55P03 'canceling statement due to lock timeout' before the lock is ever granted. This is NOT a deadlock (40P01) and NOT a DDL race (42710/23505) -- the widened lock plus pre-existing 5s lock_timeout has converted the deadlock failure mode into a lock-timeout-cancellation failure mode, still blocking TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02. Evidence: 55P03 count also trended 1 -> 4 -> 16 across the same 3 runs (inversely correlated with the deadlock count, consistent with the same underlying contention being converted from one Postgres error code to another rather than eliminated), and run 3's TC-DB-01-01 failure trace points exactly at helpers.zig:473 (`try conn.exec("SELECT pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('bpm_test_migrations_public'))", ...)`) with a 55P03 error -- the exact new acquire call this fix added. TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 did NOT pass in any of the 3 runs. SEPARATE FINDING (not part of this fix, flagged for its own issue): db_test container (port 5434) carried a stray, permanently-empty legacy `tenant_default.schema_migrations` shadow table (pre-ISS-0091 artifact, predates this run) that shadowed `public.schema_migrations` under the tenant_default,public search_path and caused runs 1-2's TC-DB-01-01/02 failures via a different mechanism (COUNT(*) resolving to the empty shadow table). This was identified via direct DB inspection, dropped mid-investigation to isolate the two failure mechanisms (run 3 was captured with it already removed, which is how the 55P03 mechanism was cleanly isolated), and is unrelated to advisory locking -- it is a latent db_integration_test.zig unqualified-table-reference bug combined with contaminated long-lived container state. CONCLUSION: per WF-03 Step 3 instructions, reporting FAIL rather than attempting an unreviewed workaround (e.g. raising lock_timeout or exempting the advisory-lock acquire statement from it) -- routing back to CODE-DESIGNER for rework, since the fix as designed does not meet the TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 acceptance bar and the design's 'Performance tradeoff' section did not account for the interaction between the widened critical section's queue depth and the pre-existing per-session lock_timeout.
